# Cross-Selling Opportunities Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Cross-Selling Opportunities Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the build Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded sales files, the proposed CRM and usage sources and the channel; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for Dynamics 365 Sales, the entitlement and usage source, the recommendation rules and Microsoft Teams; the workshop needs no connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare seller, enablement and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Commercial approval ownership | Name the account owner, sales leader, pricing reviewer and compliance reviewer who validate evidence, consent and action. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Account research effort and the expansion conversations identified by segment. Agree how expansion conversations are found today before attributing any change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Segment | Measurement period | Accounts reviewed | Research effort | Product gaps identified | Conversations started |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree data sources, rules ownership, governance, support, telemetry and success measures.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Sales business owner | Approve scope, data sources, rules and success measures; never treat synthetic scenarios as pipeline or revenue. |
| Account, pricing and compliance reviewers | Validate evidence, consent, eligibility, messaging, pricing and action before any customer engagement. |
| Recommendation rules owner | Approve replacement affinity rules and benchmarks, and resolve duplicate product recommendations. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, environment access, authenticated audience and data policies before any sales data is connected. |
| Sales data connection owners | Approve dedicated references for Dynamics 365 Sales, the entitlement and usage source and Microsoft Teams; own access failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check CS-01 through CS-04 and the boundary tests on final answers; reject reasoning text and reshoot-required captures. |
| Operations owner | Own session and credit monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route commercial decisions to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed with named owners.
- [ ] The sales owner records how expansion conversations are found today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/cross-selling/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve file, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and maker access are recorded, and the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available there.
- [ ] Authenticated seller access and only the necessary account and usage scopes are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/cross-selling/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/cross-selling/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/cross-selling/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/cross-selling/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Cross-Selling Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_cross-selling-operating-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_cross-selling-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: opportunity-scan
9. Add skill: product-affinity
10. Add skill: recommendation-engine
11. Add skill: revenue-impact
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass CS-01: Sales Operations Manager
15. Pass CS-02: Enablement Manager
16. Pass CS-03: Enablement Manager
17. Pass CS-04: Sales Leader
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: CS-01, CS-02, CS-03, CS-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The chosen lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is used, the smoke test calls `CrossSellingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in a separate fresh conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Every case is judged on the final user-facing answer, not on reasoning text.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before account or usage data is reachable. Request only read scopes for the four review skills. Restrict the seller audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Sales

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Sales — read:** Add approved Dataverse tables as knowledge or bind read-only actions; no CRM write.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Sales:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not browse, enrich or use live systems; answer from the fixed snapshot only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the missing evidence; never claim a lookup, outreach or CRM change succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Product entitlement and usage source

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data connection owners

1. **Bind Product entitlement and usage source — read:** Bind an approved read-only connector, API or MCP tool.

2. **Identity for Product entitlement and usage source:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Product entitlement and usage source:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Product entitlement and usage source:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the identifier is absent from the fixed snapshot; do not substitute another customer. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the missing evidence; never claim a lookup, outreach or CRM change succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Approved recommendation rules

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved recommendation rules — read:** Replace the rules with owner-approved knowledge and record its content owner.

2. **Identity for Approved recommendation rules:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved recommendation rules:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved recommendation rules:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no conversion, revenue or margin claim; present the labeled synthetic scenarios only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the missing evidence; never claim a lookup, outreach or CRM change succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Offer the agent in Teams after approval; gate any posting workflow separately.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send nothing and change no CRM record; return the engagement plan marked not sent. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a draft or option for authorized review and take no action.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data connection owners

Create dedicated connection references for the approved seams; do not reuse ambiguous existing connections.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved sources replace the knowledge files while preserving grounding and citation boundaries.
- [ ] Any tool replacing a recommendation-only seam has defined identity, authorization, confirmation and success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test seller and unshared identities in an approved test deployment; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Step 4-3. Deduplicate rules

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Recommendation rules owner

Deduplicate recommendations by product and re-verify scenario totals before customer evaluation.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The sales owner sets acceptance measures on customer data; synthetic affinity, response and value figures are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked sales corpus | All four cases, CS-01 through CS-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Commercial authority boundary | Any outreach, CRM change, price, quote, transaction or claimed conversion, revenue or margin outcome is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoints | Only final user-facing answers count; reasoning text, blank and reshoot-required captures cannot pass. |
| Release state | The validated manual and pilot agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before publication or any external action.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Publication and every external action have explicit user approval.
- [ ] The approved seller audience and channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, unmatched-customer answers, connection errors and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, authentication errors and credit consumption after rollout.
